h: Swap your money and spend it like a Victorian
p: One of the most loved touches at Blists Hill is the bank. You can exchange modern money for old pre-decimal coins and then spend them in the shops around town, which kids think is brilliant. Pennies and shillings suddenly make sense when you're using them to buy sweets from the counter, and grandparents tend to get a twinkle in their eye explaining how it all worked.

Food is part of the fun too. There's a traditional fish and chip shop frying the old way, a bakery and a pub, so lunch can be part of the time travel rather than a break from it. The fairground area and the shops are good for younger visitors, while older kids and adults often get absorbed watching the foundry and the craft demonstrations.

Look out for the Hay Inclined Plane right by the site, an ingenious bit of engineering where boats were lowered down the hillside to the river on rails. It's a reminder that this whole area was once an industrial powerhouse, and seeing how steep it is really brings that home.

Blists Hill is one of a family of museums across the Ironbridge Gorge. Enginuity is a hands-on design and technology centre that's great for curious kids, the Coalport China Museum and the Jackfield Tile Museum are both packed with colour, and the Tar Tunnel shows where natural bitumen oozed from the rocks. Then there's the Iron Bridge itself, opened in 1779, and the riverside town around it, which is lovely for an evening wander and a bite to eat after a day in the 1890s.
